Miettinen-Nurminen CI for the difference of two incidence rates

Source: R/eair.r
ks_eairdiff_mn.Rd

Computes the difference (Test \(-\) Control) of two exposure-adjusted incidence rates (EAIRs) and its confidence interval using the score-based method of Miettinen & Nurminen (1985).

Usage

ks_eairdiff_mn(n1, n2, T1, T2, alpha = 0.05)

Arguments

n1, n2

Non-negative integer event counts for Test and Control.

T1, T2

Positive person-time at risk for Test and Control.

alpha

Significance level for the two-sided CI. Default 0.05.

Value

A matrix with one row per input pair and three named columns: delta (point estimate), lcl (lower bound), ucl (upper bound). Bounds are NA when the score equation has fewer than two roots in (-1, 1).

Details

The CI is found by inverting the score statistic. For each candidate rate difference \(\theta\), the pooled estimate \(\tilde\lambda_2\) is obtained by solving the MLE equations under the constraint \(\lambda_1 - \lambda_2 = \theta\), and the score chi-squared is compared to \(\chi^2_{1,1-\alpha}\). The two roots of this equation (found via uniroot.all) are the lower and upper confidence bounds.

The search interval for roots is fixed at c(-1, 1), appropriate when incidence rates are measured in events per person-time unit and are well below 1. If rates exceed 1, expand the interval manually by calling uniroot.all directly.

The function is vectorised: when n1, n2, T1, T2 are vectors of equal length, one row per element is returned.

References

Miettinen O, Nurminen M (1985). Comparative analysis of two rates. Statistics in Medicine, 4(2), 213–226.

See also

ks_eairdiff_strata_mn, uniroot.all

Examples

## Single comparison: Test rate = 0.10, Control rate = 0.05
ks_eairdiff_mn(n1 = 10, n2 = 5, T1 = 100, T2 = 100)
#>      delta         lcl     ucl
#> [1,]  0.05 -0.02953395 0.13963

## Equal rates → delta = 0, CI straddles zero
ks_eairdiff_mn(n1 = 5, n2 = 5, T1 = 100, T2 = 100)
#>      delta         lcl        ucl
#> [1,]     0 -0.07307177 0.07307177

## Vectorised over multiple time-point comparisons
ks_eairdiff_mn(
  n1 = c(10, 20, 8),
  n2 = c( 5, 15, 6),
  T1 = c(100, 150, 90),
  T2 = c(100, 150, 90)
)
#>           delta         lcl       ucl
#> [1,] 0.05000000 -0.02953395 0.1396300
#> [2,] 0.03333333 -0.04641174 0.1164774
#> [3,] 0.02222222 -0.06743854 0.1163687

## 90 %% CI
ks_eairdiff_mn(n1 = 10, n2 = 5, T1 = 100, T2 = 100, alpha = 0.10)
#>      delta         lcl       ucl
#> [1,]  0.05 -0.01501574 0.1226028
